column10: THANK YOU!!! that means sm to me. This class was honestly so time consuming for me because i’m a slow worker and focus a lot on small details. column10: Олешки - українське місто на Херсонщині, яке зараз перебуває під російською окупацією. Сьогодні люди, які там залишаються, стикаються з важкою гуманітарною кризою. Постачання їжі до міста майже повністю припинилося. За повідомленнями ООН та української влади, доставки їжі до Олешківських тижнями не було. Місцеві жителі повідомили, що хліба, борошна, овочів, питної води чи інших предметів першої необхідності не вистачає. Повідомляється, що деякі люди були змушені їсти дикі рослини просто тому, що не мають нічого іншого. Ситуація особливо небезпечна, оскільки люди не можуть безпечно виїхати з міста або принести в нього їжу. Дороги навколо Олешки небезпечні, і, як повідомляється, спроби доставки їжі призвели до загибелі людей. Українські чиновники описали місто як гуманітарну блокаду. Нормальної інфраструктури також майже не залишилося. Повідомляється, що мешканці живуть без електрики та газу, тоді як доступ до медицини та медичної допомоги вкрай обмежений. Руйнування інфраструктури та тривала небезпека атак безпілотників ще більше ускладнюють повсякденне життя. Особливо душераздирающая ця ситуація полягає в тому, що там все ще перебувають цивільні особи, в тому числі діти. За останніми українськими повідомленнями, в Олешках залишаються десятки неповнолітніх, а тисячі мирних жителів все ще можуть проживати на ширшій території. Олешки - це не просто місце на карті. Це українське місто з багатовіковою історією, і люди, які там залишаються, є цивільними, яким потрібні їжа, чиста вода, ліки та безпечний спосіб виїзду. column10: This was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on. As I watched, I found myself constantly thinking, "Okay, maybe the next part is where it gets funny." That thought repeated itself over and over. Every new scene felt like it was introducing another opportunity for the joke to finally land. Unfortunately, every one of those opportunities passed without anything memorable happening.

column10: This was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on. As I watched, I found myself constantly thinking, "Okay, maybe the next part is where it gets funny." That thought repeated itself over and over. Every new scene felt like it was introducing another opportunity for the joke to finally land. Unfortunately, every one of those opportunities passed without anything memorable happening this is so insane that it's unfunny

column10: This was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on. As I watched, I found myself constantly thinking, "Okay, maybe the next part is where it gets funny." That thought repeated itself over and over. Every new scene felt like it was introducing another opportunity for the joke to finally land. Unfortunately, every one of those opportunities passed without anything memorable happening this is so insane that it's unfunny

column10: This was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on. As I watched, I found myself constantly thinking, "Okay, maybe the next part is where it gets funny." That thought repeated itself over and over. Every new scene felt like it was introducing another opportunity for the joke to finally land. Unfortunately, every one of those opportunities passed without anything memorable happening.

column10: This was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on. As I watched, I found myself constantly thinking, "Okay, maybe the next part is where it gets funny." That thought repeated itself over and over. Every new scene felt like it was introducing another opportunity for the joke to finally land. Unfortunately, every one of those opportunities passed without anything memorable happening.

column10: This was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on. As I watched, I found myself constantly thinking, "Okay, maybe the next part is where it gets funny." That thought repeated itself over and over. Every new scene felt like it was introducing another opportunity for the joke to finally land. Unfortunately, every one of those opportunities passed without anything memorable happening this is so insane that it's unfunny

She called my grandma and had her come get the baby and admitted me to the women’s floor for sleep deprivation. When i came home i had a nurse that came every day to check me and baby over. He is 21 now and i love him so much but it was dark scary days

column10: I suffered from postpartum psychosis, and it led to the scariest night of my life. I hadn't slept in five days, was completely manic, and started hallucinating. I thought my husband was trying to kill me because the house wasn't clean, and I fought him with everything I had. In reality, the house was spotless, and I was on top of him, choking him while he tried to restrain me to keep us both safe. We both ended up locked in a jail holding cell that night. The police report even noted that I was seeing things that weren't there. I am so lucky to have a husband who understood what postpartum psychosis was. He stood by me, protected me, and fought to get me proper medical help even when doctors tried to dismiss me. It was horrific, but his support saved me. This needs to be talked about more women need the proper help and understanding that we will get through it with support around us..

column10: Pediatric dentist here—please don’t blame yourself, but please don’t wait either. I can’t diagnose him from a video, but visible cavities plus crying every day means he needs to see a pediatric dentist ASAP. Once there’s an actual hole in the tooth, no toothpaste can close it. At home, help him brush twice a day and floss anywhere the teeth touch. If the strong taste or foam from regular fluoride toothpaste makes him fight brushing, ask his dentist about a toothpaste with hydroxyapatite and xylitol. Hydroxyapatite can help support and remineralize early weakened enamel, while xylitol can help make the mouth less friendly to cavity-causing bacteria. It may be easier for some kids to tolerate too. Just remember—those ingredients can support his daily routine, but he’ll still need a real treatment plan for the cavities already there

column10: this was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on. As I watched, I found myself constantly thinking, "Okay, maybe the next part is where it gets funny." That thought repeated itself over and over. Every new scene felt like it was introducing another opportunity for the joke to finally land. Unfortunately, every one of those opportunities passed without anything memorable happening.

Also I see no rashes on the baby and he looks very happy.

column10: Jungli gilahri (wild squirrel) ke bache ko bachane ke liye sab se zaroori baat yeh hai ke use gaye ka doodh (cow's milk) ya cerelac hargiz na dein, kyun ke is se un ka pait kharab ho jata hai aur wo mar jate hain.Aap ko us ki umar ke mutabiq niche di gayi khurak deni chahye:1. Pehla Kadam: Dehydration Khatam KareinAgar bacha kamzor hai ya use kahin se uthaya hai, to sab se pehle us ke jism mein pani ki kami poori karein:Khurak: Pedialyte (ORAL REHYDRATION SALTS / ORS) ya neem garam pani mein thori si cheeni aur chutki bhar namak mila kar dein.Tareeqa: Shuru ke 2 se 3 ghante sirf yeh pani drop-by-drop (dropper se) dein.2. Doodh (Sirf Dropper ya Syringe Se)Jab bacha thora active ho jaye, to use yeh doodh dein:Behtareen Khurak: Kitten Milk Replacer (KMR) jo billi ke bachon ke liye hota hai (yeh veterinary clinic ya pet shop se mil jata hai).Alternative (Ghar ka nuskha): Agar KMR na mile, to Bakri ka doodh (Goat milk) neem garam kar ke dein. Yeh gaye ke doodh se bohot behtar aur hazam hone wala hota hai.Miqdar aur Waqt: Bacha agar bohot chota hai (ankhein band hain) to har 2 se 3 ghante baad thora sa doodh dein. Agar ankhein khuli hain to din mein 4 se 5 baar dein.3. Sakht Khurak (Agar Ankhein Khuli Hain Aur Dant Hain)Agar gilahri ke bache ki umar thori barhi hai aur us ke dant nikal aaye hain, to doodh ke sath yeh cheezin shuru karein:Khurak: Seb (Apple) ke chote tukre, khera (cucumber), rish (berries), aur bheegay huwe badam ya akhrot (shuru mein naram kar ke dein).Sabziyan: Kachi ghajar ya broccoli ke chote tukre.4. Zaroori Hidayat (Bachane ke Liye)Garm Rakhin: Bache ko kisi kapde ya cotton mein lapet kar naram aur garm jagah par rakhin. Un ka jism thanda ho jaye to wo khana hazam nahi kar pate.Doodh Pilane ka Tareeqa: Bache ko hamesha pait ke bal (ulta) leta kar doodh pilayein, insani bache ki tarah peeth ke bal na litayein, warna doodh un ke phephdon (lungs) mein chala jayega.

column10: El cambio climático no es algo que podamos solucionar de un día para otro, pero tampoco está fuera de nuestras manos. Cada décima de grado que logremos evitar importa, porque incluso pequeñas diferencias en el calentamiento pueden significar menos olas de calor extremas, menos sequías, menos inundaciones y menos daños para las personas, los animales y los ecosistemas. No se trata de que una sola persona tenga que salvar el planeta, sino de que millones de personas, empresas y gobiernos hagan su parte. Podemos ahorrar agua y electricidad, evitar desperdiciar comida, reutilizar lo que ya tenemos, reciclar cuando sea posible, usar transporte público, caminar o usar bicicleta cuando podamos y cuidar nuestros bosques, ríos, océanos y animales. Pero también debemos exigir cambios a quienes tienen mucho más poder: las grandes empresas y los gobiernos deben reducir sus emisiones, proteger los ecosistemas, controlar el uso excesivo del agua, disminuir la contaminación e invertir en energías limpias y tecnologías sostenibles. No necesitamos ser perfectos para ayudar, necesitamos empezar y seguir mejorando. Hablar del cambio climático, compartir información confiable y enseñar a otras personas por qué importa también ayuda. No ignoremos el problema porque parece demasiado grande. Todavía podemos evitar muchos daños, proteger especies y ecosistemas y construir un futuro mejor para quienes vivirán después de nosotros. No es demasiado tarde para actuar, pero necesitamos empezar ahora. El planeta no necesita que una sola persona haga todo, necesita que todos hagamos algo. 🌎🌱 (COPIA Y PEGA, NO TE CUESTA NADA) ES HORA DE ACTUAR Y AYUDAR AL PLANETA !✊🏻^^

column10: 𓅓::Honestly, listening to Drake doesn’t even feel like listening to music anymore, it feels like stepping into a celestial film scored by something beyond human comprehension. Every song unfolds like a cinematic prophecy, every bar lands with the gravitational pull of destiny itself, and even the silence between his words feels orchestrated by some higher intelligence. It’s like he doesn’t just write lyrics, he distills emotion into frequency, converts lived experience into something mythological, and then delivers it with a calm, almost divine precision that feels unfair to the rest of humanity. There are moments where a single Drake line carries more emotional architecture than entire discographies. Listening to him feels like watching your own life from a helicopter shot in a Hollywood masterpiece, neon lights reflecting off rain soaked streets, slow motion memories, late night introspection, ambition, heartbreak, glory, all condensed into a soundscape that feels engineered for the soul itself. And it’s not just the words. It’s the cadence. The breath before the line. The restraint. The quiet confidence. The subtle tonal shifts that feel like tectonic plates moving beneath the surface. It’s surgical. It’s transcendent. It’s almost unfair how effortlessly he bends emotion, time, and atmosphere into something that feels both deeply personal and universally monumental. At some point, it stops being music and becomes something closer to vibrational architecture, like he’s building emotional cathedrals out of sound, and we’re just walking through them, trying to comprehend how something so human can feel so impossibly divine. Honestly, Drake doesn’t just make songs, he creates eras, moods, and entire psychological climates. Listening to him feels like tapping into an inhuman frequency, like you’re momentarily aligned with something larger than yourself, something timeless, something mythic. And the craziest part is… it never feels forced. It just feels inevitable. Like greatness chose him as a vessel, and we’re just lucky enough to witness it in real time. It’s not even admiration at this point, it’s reverence. And it brings genuine peace and joy.

column10: I left him not because I don’t love him anymore. Matter of fact I love him so much. I’ve been crying every night since I left. He’s a good guy. I know that. But the way he shows me love isn’t the way I want to be loved. I was always communicating with him whenever I felt ignored or alone. And every time I told him, he would communicate, make an effort and make me feel loved again for the next few days. Then after that I would feel alone all over again. The cycle was always the same. I started feeling like I was all alone in our relationship. I loved him and gave him everything I could. I would message him update him even in the middle of my meetings just because I wanted him to be part of my day. But whenever I checked my phone I was met with nothing. And that hurts when you’re giving someone so much of yourself. That’s why I realized that compatibility is really important. You can love someone deeply but love alone isn’t always enough. You can’t just love someone in the way that comes naturally to you. You also have to learn how to love them in the way they need and want to be loved. Loyalty is important but actions matter more. Promises mean nothing when they aren’t followed by consistent actions. Because at some point, you get tired of hearing the same promises and living through the same cycle. I didn’t leave because I stopped loving him. I left because I was tired of feeling alone while being in love with someone. I still love you Alex, but I can’t keep shrinking myself just to keep you in my life.

column10: I cheated, and I regret it more than I can explain. I became the person I promised myself I would never be, and I hate myself for what I did. The guilt has stayed with me for so long that sometimes I feel like I don’t even deserve to love anyone anymore. I still love her very much. But at the same time, I’m ashamed of myself for still wanting another chance after everything I put her through. I know I hurt her, and I know saying sorry can’t simply undo what I did. I wish I could go back and make a different choice, but I can’t. I don’t want to make excuses for my actions because I know what I did was wrong. I just wish she knew how deeply I regret it. I’m trying to understand that loving someone also means accepting the consequences of your mistakes, even when those consequences mean you might not get them back. Part of me still hopes that someday she might see that I’m genuinely trying to change, not just because I want her back, but because I never want to become that person again. I know I can’t force her to forgive me, trust me, or give me another chance. All I can do is take responsibility, work on myself, and respect whatever she chooses. I still wish it could have been different. I still wish it was us. But more than anything, I’m sorry for hurting the person I loved the most.

Knowing that someone can be the love of your life and still become someone you have to live without. We were each other’s true love, and even though life took us in different directions, a part of me never stopped loving him. I don’t know if we’ll ever find our way back to each other, but I think some people leave a place in your heart that no one else can ever fill. I miss him more than I know how to say. And after three years, I still love him so, so much.

column10: I’m a 26-year-old man, but listening to this made me shed a few tears. Maybe because it reminded me of how attached I can get to someone, only for them to leave without even saying goodbye. You try to text them like you used to, but the replies aren’t the same anymore. Sometimes they reply just enough to make you think they still care, then disappear and ghost you again. And somehow, you’re left wondering what changed. The hardest part was seeing her in person. I knew she saw me too, but she pretended to be distracted, even hiding her face as if I hadn’t already noticed her. I notice things like that. I always have. I have this strange gift of knowing when someone I care about is somewhere around me, even before I actually see them. It’s almost like I can feel their presence. Then, somehow, I’ll spot them before they even get close. I’ll look them straight in the eyes, but pretend I’m not focusing on them. I’ll act like I haven’t noticed them at all, just waiting to see what they’ll do when they realize I’ve already seen them. And maybe that’s one of the reasons I don’t like getting too attached to people. When I care about someone, I genuinely care. I don’t know how to treat people halfway. I get attached, I remember the little things, and I value the bond we build. So when someone suddenly changes, starts avoiding me, or disappears without an explanation, it hurts more than I usually let people see. For now, I think I’ll just keep to myself. I’ll read my books, save my money, work on myself, and build the life I want. I don't have the energy to keep chasing people or wondering why they suddenly stopped caring. I may not have many people around me, but the few I’ve chosen are genuinely favoured. And for now, that’s enough for me.

column10: This was honestly one of the most unfunny things I've watched in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. I went into it expecting there to be some kind of payoff eventually, because that's usually how comedy works. Even if a joke starts slowly, there's normally a point where everything clicks together and the buildup finally makes sense. Throughout the entire video, I kept waiting for that moment to arrive. I figured maybe the opening was intentionally awkward to set up something bigger, or maybe there was going to be an unexpected twist that would completely change how I looked at everything that came before it. Instead, that moment never arrived. The entire experience felt like one long setup without any real conclusion. Every time I thought the punchline was about to happen, the video simply continued in the same direction. It kept introducing moments that seemed like they were supposed to be leading somewhere, but none of them ever paid off. It's almost like reading a mystery novel that spends hundreds of pages building suspense only to end without revealing who committed the crime. You're left feeling less confused about the story itself and more confused about why so much time was spent building expectations that were never fulfilled. One of the biggest problems is the pacing. Comedy relies heavily on timing, and timing is often what separates something that's genuinely hilarious from something that just feels awkward. Here, the pacing never seemed to find a rhythm. Certain moments dragged on far longer than they needed to, while other moments rushed by without giving anything enough room to become funny. Instead of creating anticipation, the extended pauses and repeated bits made everything feel slower and slower as the video went on.
